key_insight: NeuralBES combines a shared neural encoder with a physically constrained RC thermal model so building energy forecasts stay both scalable and physics-consistent.
engineering_relevance: It offers a differentiable emulator that can support large-scale demand-side flexibility studies across diverse buildings without sacrificing the interpretability and trust of building physics.
method: Maps static building metadata to bounded RC parameters and equipment coefficients.
Solves the thermal dynamics with a log-space parallel scan for efficient full-horizon rollout.
Uses a predictor-corrector loop to handle thermostat-temperature nonlinearities while preserving gradients.
evidence_signal: Trained on ResStock across three climate zones, the model is reported to be the only data-conditioned approach that is both physics-valid and within 4 MAPE points of the strongest raw-error baseline on annual full-year rollout.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of metadata and RC parameterization, so unusual buildings or poorly specified inputs may reduce accuracy or physical validity.
paper_title: NeuralBES: A Differentiable, Control-Aware Emulator for Scalable Building Energy Modeling
